body_text:
The notation $\exists!x\in D\,P(x)$ asserts existence and
uniqueness: there is an $a\in D$ satisfying $P(a)$, and any
$b\in D$ satisfying $P(b)$ equals $a$. A proof therefore has
two logically independent parts. It is often useful to prove
uniqueness conditionally before constructing an object, because
the uniqueness argument identifies which properties a
successful construction must have.
